shortDescription: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said on Saturday that the state should secure a greater share of benefits from all mining permits and, if necessary, hold controlling stakes in mining assets.

children: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said on Saturday that the state should secure a greater share of benefits from all mining permits and, if necessary, hold controlling stakes in mining assets.

"From now on, all mining permits, at least 70% must benefit the state. If necessary, the shares should be state-controlled," he said in a speech to members of one of Indonesia's largest Islamic groups, Muhammadiyah
A statement from the presidential palace said the 70% stipulated by the president referred to the proceeds from management of mining permits
Prabowo added in his speech that Indonesia was open to investors in the mining sector but "the profits must predominantly go to the Indonesian people"

Earlier this year, several local media outlets reported, citing Deputy Energy Minister Yuliot Tanjung, that officials had discussed having the mineral and coal sector adopt a gross-split scheme under which 70% of output would go to the government and 30% to the mine operator
However, Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia later said in June that the proposal had been dropped following consultations with Prabowo
